content:
This July, Apple rolled out a basic search feature update for its TestFlight app. While you might think such a simple update would be widely welcomed, the same version of TestFlight also introduced a rather annoying bug for many users.

Personally, I wasn't significantly affected by this bug. So I view this TestFlight update as a simple yet meaningful step forward.

Sometimes a small change can have a big impact. For users with a large number of beta apps, this is especially true of Apple's latest TestFlight update. Apple has just updated TestFlight for iPhone, iPad, Mac, and more. The new version 4.3 adds a "search field to quickly find apps."

Looking back, I did notice some anomalies and noted them at the end of the article (though my judgment at the time was exactly the opposite):

I think the reason I dismissed this as a bug is that I kept years of TestFlight app records when I "merged" my separate iCloud and App Store Apple accounts last year. It wasn't convenient, but it was worth it to me.

Regardless, the TestFlight app bug didn't go unnoticed — John Vorhees at MacStories spotted it:

So when I read Zac Hall's article at 9to5Mac about TestFlight finally adding a search bar, you can imagine how excited I was. I thought to myself, "Finally!" and immediately dropped what I was doing to update the app. [...] But there's a big "however" to this story. Previously, TestFlight betas were displayed in reverse chronological order, which is how I liked it. [...] Now, expired betas are interspersed among still-valid ones, sorted alphabetically, and the list of expired betas seems to have expanded to include every beta I've ever been part of. I counted quickly, and for me that's nearly 800 app records. As you'd expect, useful betas among them are few and far between. The search function does help, but you can no longer scroll through them.

Later in August, John Gruber wrote about the TestFlight update and bug on Daring Fireball:

Last night, more than a month after the bug was introduced (and flagged by Vorhees), Apple updated TestFlight for the first time. Although the release notes only mention bug fixes, the update did address the relevant bug.

TestFlight version 4.3.1 is exactly the fix for users affected by this regression.
